rationale: Fire damage to the policyholder's own kitchen cabinets, ceiling, and walls is direct property damage to the insured residence covered under homeowners policy.
claim_summary: Grease fire in kitchen caused by sauteing; policyholder extinguished it with fire extinguisher. Kitchen cabinets above stove are charred and there is smoke damage to ceiling and walls. No injuries. Localized damage estimated in the medium range ($2,000–$25,000). Homeowners policy POL-1001 is active with $250,000 coverage limit and $500 deductible.

case_facts.description: grease fire on stove, extinguished with fire extinguisher; charred cabinets above stove and smoke damage to ceiling and walls
case_facts.damage_scope: kitchen cabinets, ceiling, walls; rest of house unaffected
case_facts.cause: grease flare-up while sauteing onions on stove

rationale: Damage to the policyholder's own home (basement flooring, drywall, and contents) caused by a burst supply line in the policyholder's own plumbing system is clearly a covered property damage claim.
claim_summary: Sam Patel's basement experienced significant water damage (approximately 2 inches throughout, with buckled hardwood flooring and drywall soaking up to 1 foot height) caused by a burst water supply line under an upstairs bathroom sink. Multiple stored boxes are also damaged. This is a high-severity property damage claim requiring urgent on-site inspection and mitigation.

rationale: Wind damage to roof shingles on the policyholder's own home is direct physical damage to the structure and falls squarely within property_damage coverage.
claim_summary: Wind damage claim for approximately four shingles blown off the back porch overhang. Estimated repair cost is $400 with no water intrusion or other damage. Low-severity claim ready for routine adjuster assignment.
